deep.reconstruction:
This page is part of Riemann's essay 'Mechanik des Ohres', published posthumously by Henle in 1867 and included in the Gesammelte Werke. It contains no formulas. It is a qualitative mechanical analysis, reconstructed below.

(a) Setup, continuing from p.12. Following Henle, the tympanic cavity is imagined rotated so that the rotation axis of the malleus–incus body runs horizontally from back to front and the oval window is vertical. The ossicular chain is a rigid body turning about this axis, with the stapes acting as a piston on the labyrinth fluid.

(b) Transmission chain. A rise in air pressure Δp_air on the drum membrane, which is fused to the malleus handle, pushes the handle inward. This presses the stapes footplate against the oval-window membrane and raises the labyrinth pressure Δp_lab. That rise drives the round-window membrane outward. In modern terms (my addition, not on the page), for small quasi-static displacements Δp_lab = G·Δp_air with a constant gain G. G is roughly the area ratio A_tm/A_ow times the lever ratio of the malleus to incus arms.

(c) Requirement of linearity. For the smallest air-pressure changes to reach the fluid 'in always the same ratio, magnified', the stapes must always act on the fluid in exactly the same way. Riemann states three necessary conditions:
1. The footplate must always press on one and the same area, and the direction of motion must stay fixed.
2. No attachments of the stapes to the window wall may noticeably affect its position or motion.
3. The stapes must never stop pressing on the oval-window membrane.
If any condition fails, the pressure changes act either not at all or under altered laws.

In modern language, condition 3 says the joint is a unilateral contact constraint. The contact force F(t) = F0 + f(t) must stay positive. Otherwise the joint separates and the map from signal to response becomes nonlinear (clipping or rectification).

(d) Preload. To secure condition 3, the tensor tympani pulls the malleus handle inward. This keeps a static pressure F0 on the oval window that considerably exceeds the largest pressure changes expected in hearing (F0 > max|f|). Riemann conjectures a feedback mechanism: the tension or curvature of the round- or oval-window membrane is sensed, and the tensor adjusts the pressure to the value most favourable for exact hearing.

(e) Equilibrium. The static pressure depends only on the position of the malleus handle. Holding a given position requires the muscle's pull (moment) to balance the moment of the tympanic-membrane tension at that position: M_muscle = M_membrane(θ0). The absolute size of the membrane tension does not matter for the preload. However, the membrane tension must stay large enough that only a very small part of the mechanical energy of the incoming wave is lost to the air inside the tympanic cavity. That argument (transmission and reflection at a stiff membrane) is carried out on p.14.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page is qualitative. Riemann's claim that the static pressure 'depends only on the position of the malleus handle' presupposes a fixed fluid/membrane stiffness, which he takes as given; this is reasonable within his quasi-static model.

The postulated sensing of window-membrane tension as a feedback signal for the tensor tympani is speculative and not borne out by later physiology. Middle-ear muscle reflexes are acoustically triggered via the brainstem, and the stapedius dominates in humans.

results.what: Conditions (fixed contact area and direction; no restraining attachments; permanent contact) for the ossicular chain to transmit pressure changes linearly with a constant gain
results.modern_name: Linearity of a unilateral-contact mechanical transmission; avoidance of contact nonlinearity (clipping) by preload
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, 'Mechanik des Ohres' (posthumous, Henle & Pfeufer's Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin, 1867); compare Helmholtz, 'Die Mechanik der Gehörknöchelchen und des Trommelfells' (1868)

results.what: Tensor tympani maintains a static preload on the stapes exceeding the maximal acoustic pressure fluctuations, possibly adjusted by sensing window-membrane tension
results.modern_name: Mechanical preload / bias point of a contact joint; middle-ear muscle tonus hypothesis
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1866/67); discussed also by Helmholtz and Politzer

results.what: Static equilibrium: muscle moment balances tympanic-membrane tension moment; membrane tension must stay large to limit energy loss to tympanic cavity air
results.modern_name: Moment balance about the ossicular rotation axis; impedance argument for transmission across a stiff membrane

deep.surprise_reason: This page is the printed text of Riemann's 'Mechanik des Ohres', published by Henle in 1867 and reprinted in Riemann's Werke. Its content is qualitative physiological mechanics already known as Riemann's.

checkable.sympy: F0, A, t = symbols('F0 A t', positive=True); f = A*sin(t); solve(F0 - A > 0, F0)
checkable.asserts: Contact force F0 + A*sin(t) stays positive for all t iff the preload F0 exceeds the amplitude A (condition 3 with tensor preload).

checkable.sympy: Atm, Aow, l1, l2, dp = symbols('A_tm A_ow l1 l2 dp', positive=True); dp_lab = dp*Atm*l1/(l2*Aow); simplify(dp_lab/dp)
checkable.asserts: Quasi-static lever/area model gives a constant pressure gain (A_tm/A_ow)*(l1/l2), independent of dp: the 'stets gleiches Verhältnis' of transmission.

checkable.sympy: Tm, rm, Tt, rt = symbols('T_m r_m T_t r_t', positive=True); solve(Eq(Tm*rm, Tt*rt), Tm)
checkable.asserts: Muscle pull needed to hold the malleus handle in position equals the membrane-tension moment divided by the muscle lever arm.
